verse: He Himself bore our sins in His body on the tree, so that we might die to sin and live to righteousness. “By His stripes you are healed.”
story: Peter is writing to servants who may be beaten for doing good, and he points them to the One who was beaten for them.

He reaches for Isaiah's song of the suffering Servant and says it plainly: Christ carried our sins Himself, in His own body, on the wood of the cross. Not a symbol of them, and not a share of them. He took them there so that sin would lose its claim on us and a new life, a righteous one, could begin. His wounds are where our healing comes from. The verse that follows says we were sheep going astray, and now we have been brought back to the Shepherd.
Lent is a road toward that tree. Bring what you are carrying today; He has already borne it.
theme: Lent: repentance, the road to the cross
